items.finding: The timing test takes the best of three runs over the SAME 1 MB string, so an implementation that memoizes on the payload makes runs 2 and 3 free and reports 0.0000 s/MB while its real first-call cost is unchanged. An adversarial validator proved this with two variants, one of them keyed on a colliding fingerprint that actually loses detection. The test shape (two 1 MB prompts, best of three) is pinned verbatim by the PRD and the design doc, so it was NOT changed. A human should decide whether to re-spec the test to time a fresh input per repetition.

The 0.3 s/MB bound sits inside the noise band of a wall-clock measurement on this machine. Measured on byte-identical code at HEAD: 0.46/0.34 (orchestrator), 0.36/0.30 and 0.43/0.36 (test author), then 0.33/0.28 and 0.17/0.13 (adversarial validator, verdict flipped from fail to pass). A 2.5x swing on the same code. As a regression pin the test will fail innocently under load and pass guiltily when idle. The PRD Risks section anticipates this and says a flake means the bound, not the code, needs review - which is a human decision, so the bound was left at the contracted 0.3.

The non-ASCII path of _normalize keeps its per-character unicodedata.category loop (_fold_run), now behind an extra regex pass, so the measured speedup applies to pure-ASCII prompts only. A prompt padded with combining marks or fullwidth text should get none of it, and nothing bounds that case: the contracted timing test uses two pure-ASCII strings. Pat (per-task review) could not measure it. Suggested fix: a second timing test over a 1 MB non-ASCII string at the same bound, and if it fails, a str.translate table for the dropped and Pd categories rather than a looser bound.

Neither rewrite in task 7 has a committed regression test. The 5.58M-case _normalize equivalence check and the 50,000-case _boundaries check ran in-process during the task and are not in the repo, so nothing stops a later edit from breaking the ASCII-run equivalence argument, and no committed test exercises overlapping spans against the shipped _boundaries. Suggested fix: a small seeded randomized test comparing both functions against inlined copies of the previous implementations, covering mixed ASCII/non-ASCII with combining marks, Pd dashes and fullwidth forms, plus overlapping and nested spans.

The large-prompt verdict test only proves there is no length cutoff up to about 295 KB, and the timing test never asserts a verdict, so a size-based early return anywhere between roughly 300 KB and 16 MB would pass every test while the acceptance criterion claims none was introduced. Pat confirmed the other four strengthening tests do bind the exploits they name. Suggested fix: extend the large-prompt test past the contract scale, or add a case with 2 MB or more of filler before the mention, asserting exit 2.

Pat raised seven LOW findings on hooks/test_read_input.py, none CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM, so per the step-5.7 ladder they were noted and not fixed in-task. Three are claims in the new module that are factually overstated and worth correcting: (1) the U+FFFD case comment says tool_name=Skill makes the hooks actually engage, but guard_phase_delegation acts on Agent, guard_push_on_critical on Bash and enforce_prd_location on file writes, so a Skill payload short-circuits most of them and those matrix cells add little beyond the empty-stdin cases - fix the claim or give each hook a payload it acts on; (2) the harness passes the REAL Path.home() as HOME while the comment says the tmp_path cwd stops a hook reaching the real repo, so a hook writing under ~ would still hit the real home - set HOME to the tmp cwd; (3) REPLACEMENT is written as a literal U+FFFD character rather than the escape \ufffd, which is invisible-prone in source. Two more: the splice test asserts only returncode==2 without checking it is the SAME deny the clean payload produces, so any other exit-2 path would pass; and the module docstring repeats itself. Pat also DISMISSED the slop pass claim that the fixture self-check assert is tautological, with a correct argument: it guards fixture drift, because if the spliced word ever left the fixture the replace would be a no-op and the returncode assertion would pass vacuously.

items.question: Task 9 requires the live replay to exit 0, but the design-doc exit rule makes that unreachable.
items.detail: The contract says exit 1 when ANY per-task/agoge/reviewer record is refused, AND separately when a pinned deny id is allowed. The pinned deny id toolu_01Ku4TbcQoeik6ZLf5XkkAuD (general-purpose, "Resume work phase for PRD 00242, task 1 onward") buckets as per-task because its description matches \btask\s+1\b, and it MUST be refused. So its correct refusal trips the first clause: exit 1 is forced no matter what the predicate does. Only three resolutions exist and the task forbids two of them (change buckets, change the deny list); the third is to exempt pinned-deny ids from the bucket-refusal clause, which cannot mask a regression (an ALLOWED pinned id still fails, a refused non-pinned per-task record still fails). Left unapplied: it is a design-doc change, not an implementor call. Verbatim contract kept, exit 1 recorded as evidence, same handling as task 7s unreachable fails-at-base criterion.
items.assumption: Replay CLI shipped verbatim to contract; exit 1 reported as a finding rather than engineered away.

items.question: The replay found six legitimate per-task dispatches the guard refuses, all because a phase name sits inside a QUOTED run.
items.detail: Measured against 1172 deduped dispatches (800 per-task): 7 per-task refusals. One is the pinned deny id (correct). The other six, with the span the guard quoted: (1) toolu_015DM18ubZLJZbA65ozvuw8c, no subagent_type, span "e-invokes `/autopilot:work`, w" - narrative prose about what re-invokes the skill. (2) toolu_013NAWvgMnP4WatpZDVyiNAa, (3) toolu_01DAQSaS3uAph2VZnfn5NC9d, (4) toolu_019nCz3WRsAZSwdaHb9itXiT, general-purpose, spans "d reports `design-solution: <p", ".assertIn(\"design-solution: <p", "ine reads `design-solution: <p" - a log-line FORMAT quoted as expected test output. (5) toolu_013ePUKbLDE7DLnbnGmgszzR, general-purpose, span "parse and plan-tasks) looks fo" - paren aside. (6) toolu_011UqbqFtUDPuSeCiLLgMvEg, autopilot:worker-opus, span "`Run the work phase for PRD 0" - this PRDs own trigger string quoted as test data, strong-anchored, and the one the session brief already records as costing a denied dispatch. Common shape: an open wrapper (backtick, double quote, paren) opens BEFORE the name and closes AFTER more text, so the name is a citation rather than the thing to run. The guard treats a wrapper as neutral: _candidates consumes a close only when it sits immediately after the name, so a longer quoted run leaves the bare name weakly anchored by the following punctuation. Five of the six also depend on per_task being false because the historical dispatch used general-purpose or no type. NOT fixed in task 9: a quoted-citation concept is a new anchoring rule in a predicate whose shape is pinned verbatim by the design doc and covered by 564 tests across three suites, so it is a design decision, not an implementor rewrite. Fixing all six would still not reach exit 0 (see the contract-conflict record), so no partial fix buys the stated goal either.
items.assumption: Predicate left exactly as tasks 5 and 6 shipped it; the six spans recorded for the design-level call.

items.question: Task 10 contracts three verbatim CHANGELOG lines, but two of them were already in the file.
items.detail: The PRD/design block tells task 10 to replace the one 00267 guard line with three verbatim lines. Tasks 3 and 4 had already landed lines two and three of that block, byte-identical, at CHANGELOG.md:17-18. Applying the contract literally left each of those two entries in the [Unreleased] / ### Fixed block TWICE (17/18 and 29/30). Both of the tasks acceptance criteria pass either way, so the criteria could not catch it; the implementor flagged it rather than de-duplicating on its own judgement, which was the right call. Resolved by the simplest safe assumption: keep the new phase-delegation-guard line, drop the two newly added duplicates, so each entry appears exactly once. The contract block itself was not edited. Verified after the fix: rg -c for the old wording exits 1, rg -c "checks sentence shape instead of word lists" prints 1, rg -c "lone surrogate" prints 1.
items.assumption: One copy of each CHANGELOG entry; the contract block read as the intended END STATE of the guard line rather than as three unconditional insertions.

items.question: dev/bin/release-checks is RED on this host, and the failures are not this PRDs.
items.detail: Final verification at db8beb0: PASS 3436 FAIL 9 SKIP 0, exit 1. All 9 reproduce identically at the PRD base b57e425 (verified in a throwaway git worktree, then removed), so none is a regression from tasks 1-10: 7 wave tests (test_wave_launch.py::test_lane_status_reports_running_while_the_pid_is_alive and ::test_lane_roots_are_distinct_registry_roots, test_wave_launch_status.py::test_status_reports_running_for_a_lane_whose_loop_is_still_alive, test_wave_launch_refusals.py::test_launch_refuses_a_checkout_a_live_loop_already_owns, test_wave_assemble.py::test_live_lane_refuses_assembly[l1/l2/l3]) plus the codex and gemini runner lane-marker shell tests. Common root cause: each resolves a live pids process NAME and gets the empty string under this sandbox (`own=<pid> cmd=  (want codex-run.sh)`), so the assertion compares against . No file any of the 9 covers is in this PRDs diff, which touches only hooks/, dev/bin/, CHANGELOG.md and the store. Consequence: the session briefs standing note that release-checks is GREEN-capable as of task 6 is STALE, and the next sessions brief must not repeat it, or a future build will read these 9 as its own regression and burn fix cycles on them. Backlog PRD 00278 (make-release-checks-tell-truth) is the natural home for the fix.
items.assumption: Phase reported with the suite red and the 9 failures named and proven pre-existing, rather than reported green or chased through step-7 fix cycles.
